title: New York's 26th Congressional District election, 2026
description: New York's 26th Congressional District covers parts of Erie and Niagara counties, including the cities of Buffalo and Niagara Falls. Incumbent Democrat Tim Kennedy, who won a special election in April 2024 to succeed longtime Representative Brian Higgins, is seeking a full term. The general election will feature Kennedy, a former state senator and occupational therapist, facing Republican challenger Dennis Hannon, a construction-business background candidate who emphasizes public safety, lower costs, and parental rights. The district leans Democratic but has competitive elements in a midterm environment where national issues and local priorities will shape the outcome.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election matchup in NY-26 as of the research date.

candidates.name: Tim Kennedy
candidates.summary: Tim Kennedy has represented New York's 26th Congressional District since May 2024, when he won a special election to succeed Brian Higgins. He previously served in the New York State Senate from 2011 to 2024, where he chaired the Transportation Committee and delivered funding for the NFTA Metro Rail. A lifelong Western New Yorker and former occupational therapist, Kennedy sits on the House Homeland Security and Veterans Affairs Committees and co-chairs the Northern Border Caucus.

candidates.name: Dennis Hannon
candidates.summary: Dennis Hannon is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Tim Kennedy for New York's 26th Congressional District. He advanced from the Republican primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled. Hannon grew up working in his father's construction business and cites his experience as a parent fighting against what he describes as medical decisions pushed on his child as a key motivation for his candidacy. His campaign focuses on public safety, reducing costs for working families, and protecting children online and in healthcare settings.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for NY-26 in the provided data, so this forecast relies entirely on structural factors and should be treated with caution. Incumbent Democrat Tim Kennedy has a recent districtwide victory (April 2024 special election) and 13 years of prior state senate service, giving him significant name recognition and institutional advantages in a district described as leaning Democratic. Republican challenger Dennis Hannon is a first-time candidate who advanced without a primary contest and lacks elected office experience. The district's description notes competitive elements in a midterm environment, which prevents a 'safe' rating. With zero polling data, a 'likely Democratic' forecast with a moderate win probability and low confidence is the most appropriate informational assessment.
